reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus holds 77 MW of published IT capacity, the second-largest among 19 Texas data centers with disclosed power, but its compliance certifications and lack of announced expansion limit its near-term AI scaling role.

The three facilities DFW3, DFW4, and DFW5 span 976,000 square feet in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro, an established power and fiber market. At 40 kW per rack, 77 MW supports roughly 1,900 racks of compute, a meaningful but not frontier-scale AI cluster. The campus's certifications, HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and SSAE 16 Type II, target regulated tenants rather than large-scale AI training, which has no standard compliance requirement. Green Globes signals energy efficiency, but power availability, not efficiency, is the binding constraint for AI.

Texas maps 133 data center sites, yet only 19 publish power capacity, totaling 475 MW. This campus accounts for 77 MW of that disclosed total, so its published capacity is material relative to what is known. The suitability score of 76 rests on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing, meaning the data shows current capacity but no signal of future growth at this location. Whether it becomes an AI scaling asset depends on unstated plans to repurpose compliance-oriented space or build new unrestricted facilities.
